steps.tx: The 2003 **ISN/RPS** classification categorizes lupus nephritis into six classes: Class I (minimal mesangial), Class II (mesangial proliferative), Class III (focal, < 50% glomeruli), Class IV (diffuse, >= 50% glomeruli), Class V (membranous), and Class VI (advanced sclerosing, >= 90% sclerosed).

vis.caption: Diffuse proliferative endocapillary hypercellularity and crescents in Class IV lupus nephritis (StewardMD).

steps.tx: **Class IV** diffuse lupus nephritis is subdivided into IV-S (segmental) and IV-G (global), displaying active wire-loop lesions (massive subendothelial deposits), hyaline thrombi, and endocapillary proliferation. The paired value for Wire-loop lesions is Thickened rigid capillary loops. The paired value for Endocapillary proliferation is Occluded capillary lumens by swollen cells.

steps.tx: Diagnostic renal biopsy reveals a '**full house**' immunofluorescence pattern, showing intense simultaneous staining for all three immunoglobulin classes (IgG, IgA, IgM) and both complement components (C3, C1q). The image is immunofluorescence microscopy showing full house staining in lupus nephritis. C1q together with all three immunoglobulins is the pattern that points to lupus.

steps.tx: First-line induction therapy for active Class III or IV lupus nephritis consists of pulse methylprednisolone followed by oral prednisone combined with either **mycophenolate mofetil** (MMF 2 to 3 g/day) or low-dose intravenous cyclophosphamide (Euro-Lupus regimen, 500 mg every 2 weeks for 6 doses).

right.title: NIH Protocol
points: 0.5 to 1.0 g/m2 monthly IV x 6 months
Elevated risk of ovarian failure and infection

steps.tx: The **BLISS-LN** trial demonstrated that adding belimumab (anti-BAFF/BLyS monoclonal antibody) to standard therapy significantly increases primary efficacy renal response and reduces renal flares and eGFR decline. The paired value for Mycophenolate mofetil is 2 to 3 g/day divided oral. The paired value for Euro-Lupus Cyclophosphamide is 500 mg IV every 2 weeks x 6.

steps.tx: The **AURINIA trial** established that triple therapy incorporating voclosporin (a novel calcineurin inhibitor) with MMF and low-dose steroids significantly doubles complete renal response rates in active lupus nephritis. The first step is Severe proliferative lupus nephritis. The next step is Initiate background MMF and glucocorticoids.

steps.tx: **Hydroxychloroquine** is recommended for all patients with lupus nephritis unless contraindicated, significantly reducing renal flare rates, chronic kidney damage accrual, thrombotic events, and all-cause mortality. One side is Belimumab (BLISS-LN), and the other side is Rituximab (LUNAR). A key point is Inhibits soluble BLyS / BAFF cytokine.

steps.tx: **National** Institutes of Health (NIH) activity index (scored 0 to 24, including endocapillary hypercellularity, karyorrhexis, crescents double-weighted) and chronicity index (scored 0 to 12, including glomerulosclerosis, interstitial fibrosis) guide treatment intensity and reversibility. The first step is All patients with lupus nephritis.
